spotVsFutures.q: Spot vs futures: what's the difference?
spotVsFutures.a: Spot means you own the asset — sell higher to profit, and you can only lose what you paid. Futures is margin trading: you never hold the underlying, you can go long or short, leverage amplifies exposure, and you can be liquidated. Gold and oil here are futures-only (TradFi perpetuals) with no spot to buy; tokenized US equities are spot.

leverage.a: One unit of capital controls several times its size. Open 10x on 100 USDT and you hold a 1,000 USDT position — every 1% move in price is 10% on your capital. Losses are magnified exactly as much as gains, and the higher the multiple the closer liquidation gets. Futures here use tiered leverage (each tier caps position size); spot buys also offer low-multiple borrowed leverage, charged daily.

crossVsIsolated.q: Cross vs isolated margin: what's the difference?
crossVsIsolated.a: It comes down to what pays for the loss. Isolated: each position stakes only its own margin, so the worst case is that one slice and the rest of your funds are untouched. Cross: the whole available balance backs every position, so one loser eats into the entire account — it survives bigger swings, but liquidation costs far more. Start with isolated, where the maximum loss is obvious.

markPrice.q: What is the mark price, and why does liquidation use it?
markPrice.a: A fair price the exchange derives from the composite spot index. It is smoother than the last traded price, and it is what unrealized PnL and liquidation triggers are computed from. That stops anyone pushing the traded price through a thin book with one big order to liquidate others on purpose (a wick). Your position PnL tracks the mark price, not the latest candle price.

liqPrice.q: How is the liquidation price worked out?
liqPrice.a: When the mark price reaches it, the system force-closes your position. Intuitively it is the price where your margin is nearly used up, minus one more cushion for the maintenance margin rate (MMR). Higher leverage and thinner margin put it closer to your entry. The order panel estimates it live; once you hold a position, switch on position lines in the chart toolbar to draw entry, TP/SL and liquidation onto the chart.

mmr.q: What is the maintenance margin rate (MMR)?
mmr.a: The minimum margin ratio a position needs to avoid liquidation. It is tiered by notional value: bigger position, higher tier, higher MMR — large positions are harder to unwind, so they must carry a thicker cushion. Liquidation triggers when margin + unrealized PnL < position value × MMR.

fundingRate.q: What is the funding rate, and why does holding cost money?
fundingRate.a: Perpetual futures never settle, so funding tethers the contract price to spot: a positive rate means longs pay shorts, a negative one the reverse. It is charged three times a day (aligned with Binance settlement times) on notional value, at the live Binance rate for the current period, falling back to a fixed +0.01% only if the feed fails. This is the main cost of holding a position for a long time — the position card shows the estimate for each period.

tpSl.q: How do take profit and stop loss work?
tpSl.a: Every futures position can carry several TP/SL levels, each with its own price and size. When the mark price reaches one it fills at market and you get a notification. Getting stopped out is nothing to be ashamed of — the campaign awards points for it under "Stop-loss hero". Decide your exit before you enter: liquidation is losing by default, a stop loss is losing on your own terms.

doubleLiq.q: What is a long-short double liquidation?
doubleLiq.a: The liquidation feed shows force-closed orders from across the site, including the Binance liquidation stream. In violent moves one side goes first — a sharp drop takes out the longs — then the snap-back takes out everyone who chased the short. That is a long-short double liquidation, often read as a sign of extreme sentiment and a possible short-term reversal.

bankrupt.q: What happens if I go bankrupt?
bankrupt.a: When your trading net worth (cash + position value − borrowed principal and interest) falls below zero, you are marked bankrupt: all wallets and positions are cleared and your starting capital is restored the next trading day. An automatic recovery still counts against your weekly resets — during the campaign, going bankrupt after you have already reset this week is charged as a paid reset, 30 campaign points.

prediction.q: How does the prediction market work?
prediction.a: You bet on future events with the game wallet: the price is the probability the market implies, so buy the side you believe in and hold to settlement, which pays 1 if you were right and 0 if not. You can also sell early to lock in the result. During the campaign, single bets of 100 or more held to a winning settlement earn campaign points, subject to tiered caps — it is not farmable.

dailyVote.q: What is the daily long-short vote?
dailyVote.a: Each day you vote on whether BTC and gold go up or down tomorrow. The target is tomorrow's UTC daily candle and voting closes tonight, so there is no hindsight; it settles on the daily close after 08:00 the next morning. A pool of 100 points a day is split among everyone who was right — the crowded side gets less per head, a correct contrarian call more — capped at 6 points per person per day.

wallets.q: Are the game wallet and the trading wallet the same?
wallets.a: No. The main wallet is for trading (spot, futures, stocks); the game wallet funds Mines, Video Poker, Blackjack and the prediction market. They are accounted for separately, with an entry to transfer between them. Bankruptcy is judged on trading net worth alone — the game wallet cannot save you, and it is wiped along with everything else.

coupon.a: Tick a coupon from the daily buff draw when you place a spot market buy and it cuts the fill amount by the coupon rate. The "Saved" figure on the leaderboard totals what you have discounted this way. The rarer the coupon, the steeper the discount — keep the legendary ones for large orders.

campaign.q: What are campaign points and the LDC prize pool?
campaign.a: During the five-dimension trading contest you earn points from trading (ROI targets and net PnL), the daily check-in, the long-short vote, the prediction market, comments and more; the campaign page lists every task and your live breakdown. Liquidations and the like deduct points. When it ends, the LDC prize pool is split by final point weight — authorize your LinuxDo account on the campaign page to claim. Resetting your account does not clear points already earned.

resetAccount.q: What are the rules for resetting my account?
resetAccount.a: A reset clears all positions, orders, game records and asset history and returns your balance to the starting capital; comments, mute status and campaign points are unaffected. During the campaign the first reset each calendar week is free, every one after that costs 30 campaign points; after the campaign it is one per week, refreshed on Monday. An automatic bankruptcy recovery counts toward the same quota.
